newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea indicts 438 students over violent protests.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea indicts 438 students over violent protests.

text.p: South Korean prosecutors on Tuesday charged 438 radical students en masse with being involved in recent violent demonstrations in which a policeman was killed, a Seoul prosecution official said.
The official said the indicted youths were among some 5,850 student activists detained by police during the protests last month to back calls unity with communist North Korea.

Most of the students were charged with involvement in nine days of pro-unification agitation at Seoul's Yonsei University, which was masterminded by the outlawed Hanchongryon, or the Korean Federation of University Student Councils.

Riot police ended the protests by storming a teaching block at the campus used by the students as a stronghold. Hundreds of students and riot police were wounded in pitched battles, and one young police officer died of head wounds.
"The number of indicted students is the highest ever in a single incident in our history," the prosecution official said.

The previous record was registered in 1986 when 395 students were indicted for taking part in three days of violent anti-government protests at another Seoul university campus under the military-backed rule of then president Chun Doo Hwan.

The official said 38 of the students indicted on Tuesday were also charged with violating the nation's security law, which bans any contacts or exchanges with the communist North, still technically at war with the South since the 1950-53 Korean conflict.
Ten others were charged with accidental homicide, stemming from the death of the police officer.

The clashes at Yonsei were the worst violence since Presidnt Kim Young-sam took power in February 1993. Following the Yonsei incidents, Kim accused radical students of waging urban guerrilla warfare in support of Pyongyang and vowed to sternly punish North Korean sympathisers.
